z_path = doleans_exponential(x_path)
recovered_x = stochastic_logarithm(z_path)

# Verify whether simulated paths form a true martingale
defect_res = martingale_defect(all_paths, times)
print(f"Is true martingale: {defect_res.is_true_martingale}")

docs.title: 4. Girsanov Measure Transformations (spxa.calculus.girsanov)
docs.text:
Implements the Cameron-Martin-Girsanov theorem:

\[Z_t = \left. \frac{d\mathbb{Q}}{d\mathbb{P}} \right|_{\mathcal{F}_t} = \exp\left( -\int_0^t \theta_s dW_s^\mathbb{P} - \frac{1}{2} \int_0^t |\theta_s|^2 ds \right)\]

Shifts Brownian drift under risk-neutral (\(\mathbb{Q}\)), \(T\)-forward (\(\mathbb{Q}^T\)), and annuity measures, and reweights pathwise expectations via importance sampling:

\[\mathbb{E}^\mathbb{Q}[\Phi(S_T)] = \mathbb{E}^\mathbb{P}[\Phi(S_T) Z_T]\] 
from spxa.calculus.girsanov import risk_neutral_measure_change

rn_change = risk_neutral_measure_change(
    physical_drift=0.12,
    volatility=0.20,
    risk_free_rate=0.05
)

# Transform expectations under Physical measure into Risk-Neutral prices
rn_price = rn_change.expectation_change(call_payoffs, radon_nikodym_densities)

docs.title: 5. Infinitesimal Generators & Dynkin Solvers (spxa.calculus.generator)
docs.text:
Evaluates the differential operator \(\mathcal{A} f(x) = b(x) f'(x) + \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2(x) f''(x)\) and solves boundary value problems via scale and speed measures:

\[s'(x) = \exp\left(-\int_a^x \frac{2 b(y)}{\sigma^2(y)} dy\right), \quad m(x) = \frac{2}{\sigma^2(x) s'(x)}\]
  • Dynkin Mean First Exit Time: Solves \(\mathcal{A} u(x) = -1\) on \((a, b)\) with \(u(a) = u(b) = 0\): $\(u(x) = \frac{s(x) - s(a)}{s(b) - s(a)} \int_a^b (s(b) - s(y)) m(y) dy - \int_a^x (s(x) - s(y)) m(y) dy\)$
  • Feller Boundary Classification: Classifies boundaries into Regular, Exit, Entrance, or Natural.
from spxa.calculus.generator import (
    classify_feller_boundary,
    dynkin_mean_exit_time,
    dynkin_exit_probability
)

# Mean first exit time for standard Brownian motion on [-1, 1]
x_grid, u_vals = dynkin_mean_exit_time(lambda x: 0.0, lambda x: 1.0, a=-1.0, b=1.0)
# u(0) = 1.0 (exact theoretical value)

# Feller classification for CIR at boundary 0
feller_res = classify_feller_boundary(
    drift_fn=lambda x: 2.0 * (0.04 - x),
    diffusion_fn=lambda x: 0.1 * (x ** 0.5),
    boundary_point=0.0,
    interior_point=0.04
)
print(feller_res.classification)  # BoundaryType.ENTRANCE

docs.title: 6. Realized Quadratic Variation & Jump Tests (spxa.calculus.variation)
docs.text:
Computes realized quadratic variation, covariation, and Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard realized bipower variation (BV) to separate continuous diffusive volatility from jumps:

\[\text{BV}_t = \frac{\pi}{2} \sum_{k=2}^n |\Delta X_k| \cdot |\Delta X_{k-1}| \xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}} \int_0^t \sigma_s^2 ds\]

Provides statistical hypothesis tests: - BNS \(Z\)-Test: Tests \(H_0: \text{No jumps}\) against \(H_1: \text{Jumps present}\). - Lee-Mykland Test: Intraday identification of jump arrival times and magnitudes using local bipower volatility and Gumbel thresholds.

from spxa.calculus.variation import bns_jump_test, lee_mykland_jump_test

bns_res = bns_jump_test(price_series, alpha=0.01)
print(f"Jumps detected: {bns_res.has_jumps}, p-value: {bns_res.p_value}")

lm_res = lee_mykland_jump_test(price_series, times, alpha=0.01)
print(f"Detected jump timestamps: {lm_res.jump_times}")

docs.title: 7. Local Times & Tanaka's Formula (spxa.calculus.local_time)
docs.text:
Estimates semimartingale local time \(L_t^a(X)\) via Meyer's mollified Gaussian kernel estimator:

\[L_t^a(X) = \lim_{\epsilon \downarrow 0} \frac{1}{2\epsilon} \int_0^t \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_s - a| < \epsilon\}} d[X, X]_s\]

Verifies Tanaka's formula decomposition for call and absolute value payoffs:

\[(X_t - a)^+ = (X_0 - a)^+ + \int_0^t \mathbf{1}_{\{X_s > a\}} dX_s + \frac{1}{2} L_t^a(X)\]

and validates the occupation times identity:

\[\int_0^T \mathbf{1}_{\{a \le X_s \le b\}} d[X, X]_s = \int_a^b L_T^u(X) du\] 
from spxa.calculus.local_time import tanaka_decomposition, verify_occupation_times_formula

tanaka = tanaka_decomposition(path, level=0.0)
print(f"Accumulated local time at zero: {tanaka.tanaka_local_time[-1]}")

lhs, rhs, rel_err = verify_occupation_times_formula(path, lower_bound=-0.5, upper_bound=0.5)

docs.title: 8. Malliavin Variational Calculus (spxa.calculus.malliavin)
docs.text:
Provides variational calculus on Wiener space \(\mathbb{D}^{1,2}\): - First Variation Process \(Y_t = \frac{\partial X_t}{\partial x_0}\): Linearized tangent SDE. - Malliavin Derivative \(D_s X_t = Y_t Y_s^{-1} \sigma(X_s) \mathbf{1}_{\{s \le t\}}\). - Bismut-Elworthy-Li Formula: Computes exact Greeks for non-differentiable / digital payoffs without differentiation: $\(\nabla_x \mathbb{E}[\Phi(X_T)] = \frac{e^{-rT}}{T} \mathbb{E}\left[ \Phi(X_T) \int_0^T \sigma^{-1}(X_t) Y_t dW_t \right]\)$ - Clark-Ocone Formula: Explicit replicating portfolio delta representation: $\(\Delta_0 = \frac{e^{-rT}}{\sigma S_0 T} \mathbb{E}[\Phi(S_T) W_T]\)$

from spxa.calculus.malliavin import bismut_elworthy_li_delta, clark_ocone_hedging_delta

# Calculate Delta for a discontinuous Digital Call Option (1_{S_T >= K})
bismut_res = bismut_elworthy_li_delta(
    paths=s_paths,
    terminal_payoff=(s_paths[:, -1] >= K).astype(float),
    times=times,
    bm_increments=dw,
    diffusion_func=lambda t, s: sigma * s,
    discount_factor=np.exp(-r * T)
)
print(f"Exact Digital Delta: {bismut_res.greek_value} +/- {bismut_res.standard_error}")

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to spxa are documented here. Follows Keep a Changelog and Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• pde/ — finite-difference PDE and PIDE solvers (spxa.pde, spxa.graph.pde). Every scheme is covered by a convergence test against a closed form or a published reference. Contents:
  • Infrastructure.
    • Grids: uniform and sinh-stretched Grid1D with strikes, barriers and spots placed on nodes; TimeGrid with calendar events.
    • Boundary conditions: Dirichlet, Neumann, linear and natural.
    • Operators and time stepping: second-order DiscreteOperator1D with automatic upwinding; ThetaSolver1D (Crank–Nicolson with Rannacher start-up); payoff projection.
    • Results: grid Greeks and __story__() summaries.
  • Early exercise. PenaltyLCP, PSORLCP, BrennanSchwartzLCP and IkonenToivanenLCP, plus complementarity_residual and recorded exercise boundaries.
  • One-factor pricers.
    • BlackScholesPDE: European, digital, American, Bermudan, single, double and discretely monitored barriers, discrete dividends, local volatility, and bumped vega/rho.
    • DupirePDE and local_vol_from_prices.
    • AsianPDE (Večeř; continuous and discrete averages).
    • ShortRatePDE (Vasicek/CIR bonds and European/American bond options).
  • Generators and densities.
    • to_pde and Process.to_pde(): diffusion generators and exponential-Lévy PIDEs.
    • FokkerPlanck1D: a discrete-adjoint density solver that conserves mass to machine precision.
  • Lévy PIDEs. LevyJumpOperator (cell-integrated large jumps, moment-matched small jumps, FFT convolution) and LevyPIDE for European and American options under Merton, Kou, VG, CGMY and NIG.
  • Two-factor ADI.
    • Building blocks: Grid2D, Dirichlet2D/Neumann2D/Natural2D/Linear2D, LinearPDE2D, DiscreteOperator2D.
    • ADISolver: Douglas, Craig–Sneyd, modified Craig–Sneyd and Hundsdorfer–Verwer, with damping steps and Ikonen–Toivanen early exercise.
    • HestonPDE: European and American, with Greeks and vega.
    • TwoAssetBlackScholesPDE: exchange, spread, best-of and worst-of options, European or American.
  • Cross-checks and bridges.
    • longstaff_schwartz and lsm_american: two-pass least-squares Monte Carlo.
    • pde_price and pde_pricing_fn: price spxa.risk instruments and feed StressTestingEngine.
    • spxa.graph.pde.bs_pde_price_node and heston_pde_price_node: graph nodes whose vector–Jacobian products use the grid Greeks.
  • Verification.
    • Convergence tools: convergence_study, observed_order and richardson_extrapolate.
    • Closed-form references in spxa.pde.reference: Black–Scholes, Reiner–Rubinstein, binomial trees, perpetual put, Lewis with Heston/Lévy characteristic functions, Merton series, Vasicek/CIR bonds and options, Margrabe, spread options.
  • Documentation. See docs/theory/pde.md and section 19 of the API reference.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• zoo.levy.CGMY: the Lévy density, total mass, tail and drift now temper upward jumps with \(M\) and downward jumps with \(G\), as the characteristic exponent does; previously they described the mirror-image process. For \(1 \le Y < 2\) the drift now includes the \(-\int_{|x|>1} x\,\nu(dx)\) correction. The first cumulant is no longer rejected as nonexistent when \(\Gamma(1-Y)\) is finite.
  • zoo.levy.NIG: the triplet drift and tail integrated the NIG probability density instead of the Lévy density. The drift now follows from \(\mathbb{E}[X_1] = \mu + \delta\beta/\gamma\), and the tail integrates the Lévy density.
  • zoo.levy.KouJumpDiffusion: char_func now uses the closed-form exponent. The inherited numerical Lévy–Khintchine integral returned nan at complex arguments such as \(u = -i\).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• morph/ — Model Morphing (spxa.morph, spxa.graph.morph): continuous interpolation between processes. The triplet homotopy \(\psi_\alpha = (1-\alpha)\psi_0 + \alpha\psi_1\) is EXACT for Lévy processes. Also includes generator, Fisher–Rao geodesic, Wasserstein and convex-combination morphs; time- and state-dependent schedules (DynamicMorphedProcess); ModelBarycenter, ModelEnsemble and SurfaceMorphEngine; and the Process.morph / spxa.morph API. See docs/theory/model_morphing.md.
  • zoo/beyond/multivariate_hawkes.py — Multivariate Hawkes mutually exciting point process (MultivariateHawkesProcess, MultivariateHawkes, MHawkes): \(M\)-dimensional Hawkes intensity \(\lambda_m(t)\), branching infectivity matrix \(\mathbf{\Gamma}\), spectral radius stationarity condition \( ho(\mathbf{\Gamma}) < 1\), exact expected arrival intensity \(\mathbf{\lambda}_\infty = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{\Gamma})^{-1} \mathbf{\mu}\), and Ogata thinning event simulation.
  • zoo/levy/nts.py — Normal Tempered Stable (NTS) Lévy process (NormalTemperedStableProcess, NormalTemperedStable, NTSProcess): Subordinated Brownian motion \(X_t = heta T_t + \sigma W(T_t)\) with Tempered Stable subordinator, exact closed-form characteristic function, exact cumulant generating function, and subordination simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/kou_sv.py — Kou Stochastic Volatility Jump-Diffusion model (KouSVProcess, KouSV, KouStochasticVolatility): Coupled Heston mean-reverting stochastic volatility with Kou asymmetric double-exponential jumps, affine characteristic function, Lewis Fourier inversion European call/put options, and full-truncation Euler simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/diffusion_bridge.py — General Diffusion Bridge via Doob's \(h\)-transform (GeneralDiffusionBridge, DiffusionBridge, DoobBridge): Drift correction \(\mu^*(x, t) = \mu(x) + \sigma^2(x) \partial_x \ln p(b, T \mid x, t)\) for Brownian, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, and Geometric Brownian Motion bridges, exact moments, and pinned path simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/rough_heston.py — Rough Heston stochastic volatility model (RoughHestonProcess, RoughHeston, RoughVolatility): Fractional Volterra stochastic volatility of order \(\alpha = H + 1/2 \in (1/2, 1)\), singular kernel \(K(t) = t^{\alpha - 1} / \Gamma(\alpha)\), Mittag-Leffler expected variance, power-law implied volatility skew \(|\partial \sigma_{IV} / \partial k| \sim T^{H - 0.5}\), and fractional convolution simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/g2pp.py — Two-Factor Hull–White (G2++) short-rate diffusion model (G2PlusPlusProcess, G2PlusPlus, TwoFactorHullWhite): Two coupled OU factors driving short rate \(r(t) = x(t) + y(t) + \phi(t)\), closed-form zero-coupon bond pricing \(P(t, T)\), Brigo–Mercurio European bond option formulas, and exact bivariate Gaussian factor simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/three_halves.py — 3/2 Stochastic Volatility diffusion model (ThreeHalvesProcess, ThreeHalves, ThreeHalvesModel): Super-linear volatility-of-variance \(dv_t = \kappa v_t ( heta - v_t) dt + \epsilon v_t^{3/2} dW_t\), exact reciprocal CIR transformation \(y_t = 1/v_t\) with automatic Feller satisfaction, Inverse-Gamma stationary law, and exact non-central chi-square path simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/schwartz_one_factor.py — Schwartz One-Factor (1997) commodity diffusion model (SchwartzOneFactor, ExponentialOU, Schwartz1F): Mean-reverting log-spot Ornstein–Uhlenbeck dynamics, exact lognormal transition law and moments, closed-form commodity futures price term structure \(F(t, T)\), and Black-76 European options on futures.
  • zoo/beyond/garch_diffusion.py — Nelson (1990) continuous-time GARCH(1,1) diffusion limit (GARCHDiffusion, ContinuousGARCH, GARCHDiffusionProcess): Linear diffusion coefficient \(g(v) = \sigma v\), exact Inverse-Gamma stationary distribution, conditional moments from linear moment ODE system, and guaranteed-positive log-Euler simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/bilinear.py — Bilinear Diffusion process (BilinearDiffusion, BilinearDiffusionProcess, AffineDiffusion): Affine drift and affine volatility \(dX_t = (a + b X_t) dt + (c + d X_t) dW_t\), Pearson diffusion family moments, exact second-moment ODE solution, and high-order Milstein boundary simulation.
  • vis/levy_inspector.py — Lévy triplet diagnostic inspector and dual-panel density visualizer: Decomposes \((b, \sigma^2, u)\), classifies finite activity (\(\int u(dx) < \infty\)) vs infinite activity (\( u(\mathbb{R}) = \infty\)), finite vs infinite path variation, estimates Blumenthal-Getoor index \( eta \in [0, 2]\) and singularity order \(s\), and plots near-zero singularity zoom vs tail decay on semi-log scale.
  • vis/surface.py — 3D implied volatility surface and cross-model smile visualizer: Computes and renders 3D \((K, T, \sigma_{\mathrm{IV}})\) surfaces with isoline contours, cross-model smile comparison curves across diffusions, jumps, and stochastic volatility models, and volatility term structure plots.
  • vis/story_dag.py — Process composition DAG visualizer and multi-format exporter: Walks CompositionNode trees and exports to ASCII / Unicode tree structures, Mermaid flowcharts for Markdown previews, Graphviz DOT files, and publication-quality hierarchical NetworkX + Matplotlib diagrams.
  • vis/__init__.py — Unified visualization namespace exposing all diagnostic, surface, and DAG tools.
  • examples/visualization_example.py — End-to-end demonstration script generating sample plots and diagrams.
  • tests/unit/test_vis.py — Comprehensive unit test suite for all visualization submodules.
  • sim/milstein.py — High-order 1D and multivariate commutative Milstein simulation schemes: Order 1.0 strong convergence with analytical or automatic centered finite-difference diffusion derivatives.
  • sim/runge_kutta.py — Derivative-free Stochastic Runge-Kutta schemes: Strong order 1.0 Kloeden-Platen scheme (matching Milstein accuracy without diffusion derivatives) and weak order 2.0 scheme for expectation evaluation.
  • sim/qmc.py — Quasi-Monte Carlo simulation engine: Sobol and Halton low-discrepancy sequences, Owen scrambling, and hierarchical Brownian bridge path construction.
  • sim/variance_reduction.py — Comprehensive variance reduction toolkit: Optimal single/multivariate control variate regression estimator, antithetic Gaussian and Brownian paths, Girsanov importance sampling with Radon-Nikodym likelihood weights, and 1D stratified uniform sampling.
  • sim/predictor_corrector.py — Drift-implicit predictor-corrector schemes for stiff SDEs: Unconditionally stable trapezoidal integration for stiff mean-reverting processes.
  • sim/mlmc.py — Giles (2008) Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) framework: Optimal \(O(\epsilon^{-2})\) estimation complexity, adaptive level selection, and optimal variance allocation.
  • examples/simulation_backends_example.py — Comprehensive demonstration of all advanced simulation backends.
  • zoo/beyond/cbi.py — CBISubordinator (CBIProcess, DawsonWatanabeProcess, ContinuousStateBranching): Dawson-Watanabe continuous-state branching process with continuous and jump immigration (Kawazu & Watanabe 1971; Dawson & Li 2012): \(dX_t = (a - b X_t) dt + \sqrt{c X_t} dW_t + dJ_t\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact closed-form Riccati solution \(v(t, \lambda)\), affine Laplace transform \(\mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda X_t}]\), exact conditional mean and variance with compound Poisson immigration, analytical extinction probability for pure CSBP, and high-order Milstein simulation with non-negative reflection. References: Kawazu & Watanabe (1971); Dawson & Li (2012); Li (2011); Grey (1974).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_cbi Dawson-Watanabe Milstein sampler with jump immigration.
  • zoo/beyond/chen.py — ChenModel (ChenThreeFactor, ChenShortRate, ChenProcess): Chen (1996) three-factor interest rate model with stochastic central tendency (mean) and stochastic variance: \(dr_t = k ( heta_t - r_t) dt + \sqrt{\zeta_t r_t} dW_{1,t}\), \(d heta_t = \kappa ( ar{ heta} - heta_t) dt + \alpha \sqrt{ heta_t} dW_{2,t}\), \(d\zeta_t = \lambda ( ar{\zeta} - \zeta_t) dt + eta \sqrt{\zeta_t} dW_{3,t}\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact closed-form expectations, Feller condition analytics, exact 10-dimensional matrix exponential moment system for second moments and conditional variance, term structure zero-coupon bond pricing and yield curve, and coupled 3-factor simulation. References: Chen (1996).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_chen coupled 3-factor path sampler.
  • zoo/beyond/regime_switching_gbm.py — RegimeSwitchingGBM (RSGBM, RegimeSwitchingBlackScholes, MarkovSwitchingGBM): Continuous-time Markov-modulated Black-Scholes diffusion of Hamilton (1989), Naik (1993), and Guo (2001): \(dS_t = \mu(Y_t) S_t dt + \sigma(Y_t) S_t dW_t\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact CTMC transition probabilities \(P(t) = \exp(Q t)\), stationary probability distribution \( oldsymbol{\pi}\), arbitrary order exact matrix exponential moments \(\mathbb{E}[S_t^n \mid S_0, Y_0]\), continuous characteristic function via matrix exponentials, closed-form Gil-Pelaez European call and put option pricing with machine-precision put-call parity, and coupled Markov-jump and diffusion path simulation. References: Hamilton (1989); Naik (1993); Guo (2001); Elliott, Aggoun, & Moore (1994).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_regime_switching_gbm coupled Markov chain and diffusion path sampler.
  • zoo/beyond/jacobi.py — JacobiProcess (JacobiDiffusion, WrightFisherDiffusion, Jacobi): Jacobi bounded diffusion model on \([y_{\min}, y_{\max}]\) (canonical \([0, 1]\)) of Ackerer, Filipović, & Turnes (2018): \(dY_t = \kappa ( heta - Y_t) dt + \sigma \sqrt{ rac{(Y_t - y_{\min})(y_{\max} - Y_t)}{y_{\max} - y_{\min}}} dW_t\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact Beta stationary law \(\mathrm{Beta}(\alpha, eta)\), exact polynomial moment propagation (mean, second moment, and conditional variance), Feller boundary classifications at both lower and upper endpoints (entrance vs regular reflecting), and high-order Milstein path simulation with strict boundary preservation. References: Ackerer, Filipović, & Turnes (2018); Karlin & Taylor (1981); Filipović & Larsson (2016).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_jacobi Milstein path simulator for bounded intervals.
  • zoo/beyond/bns.py — BNSModel (BNSProcess, BarndorffNielsenShephard, BNS): Non-Gaussian Ornstein-Uhlenbeck stochastic volatility model of Ole E. Barndorff-Nielsen & Neil Shephard (2001): \(dX_t = (\mu + eta \sigma_t^2) dt + \sigma_t dW_t + ho dZ_{\lambda t}, \quad d\sigma_t^2 = -\lambda \sigma_t^2 dt + dZ_{\lambda t}\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features Gamma-OU variance driven by a compound Poisson BDLP \(Z_t\) with rate \(\alpha\) and exponential jump size \( eta_{bdlp}\), exact stationary variance distribution \(\Gamma(\alpha, eta_{bdlp})\), exact conditional and integrated variance moments, continuous Fourier characteristic function \(\phi(u; t)\), European call/put option pricing via Gil-Pelaez inversion with exact Put-Call parity, Black-Scholes implied volatility smile computation, and coupled vectorized simulation. References: Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard (2001); Nicolato & Venardos (2003); Schoutens (2003).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_bns coupled asset price and stochastic variance simulator.
  • zoo/beyond/schwartz_two_factor.py — SchwartzTwoFactor (Schwartz97, Schwartz2F, SchwartzTwoFactorModel): Canonical two-factor commodity pricing model of Eduardo Schwartz (1997) with mean-reverting convenience yield: \(dS_t = (r - \delta_t) S_t dt + \sigma_1 S_t dW_1^Q(t), \quad d\delta_t = \kappa (\hat{\alpha} - \delta_t) dt + \sigma_2 dW_2^Q(t)\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact closed-form futures pricing \(F(S_t, \delta_t, au)\) via Schwartz (1997) Proposition 1 eq. (12), exact conditional Gaussian moments for convenience yield \(\delta_t\) and log-spot \(X_t = \ln S_t\), exact characteristic function \(\phi(u; t)\), analytical Black-76 European call and put options with exact Put-Call parity, and joint vectorized path simulation of spot prices and convenience yields. References: Schwartz (1997); Bjerksund (1991).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_schwartz_two_factor joint spot and convenience yield simulator.
  • zoo/beyond/jcir.py — JCIRProcess (JCIR, JumpCIRProcess, JCIRModel): Jump-Extended Cox-Ingersoll-Ross short-rate model of Duffie & Garleanu (2001) and Maghsoodi (1996): \(dr_t = \kappa ( heta - r_t) dt + \sigma \sqrt{r_t} dW_t + dJ_t, \quad r_0 \ge 0\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features non-negative interest rates with compound Poisson exponential jump shocks (\(Y_i \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\mu_J)\)), exact stationary mean \( heta_\infty = heta + (\lambda_J \mu_J)/\kappa\) and stationary variance, exact conditional moments at any horizon, closed-form exponential-affine zero-coupon bond pricing \(P(t, T) = \exp(A( au) - B( au) r_t)\) with exact analytical Riccati integration, term structure yields, analytical instantaneous forward rates, exact conditional characteristic function, and exact simulation combining non-central \(\chi^2\) CIR transitions with compound Poisson jump increments. References: Duffie & Garleanu (2001); Maghsoodi (1996); Brigo & Mercurio (2006).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_jcir exact non-central chi-squared + compound Poisson jump simulator.
  • zoo/beyond/bessel.py — SquaredBesselProcess (BESQ, SquaredBessel) and BesselProcess (BES, Bessel): Canonical squared Bessel and Bessel diffusion processes of Feller (1951), Pitman & Yor (1982), and Revuz & Yor (1999): \(dX_t = \delta dt + 2\sqrt{X_t} dW_t, \quad R_t = \sqrt{X_t}, \quad dR_t = rac{\delta - 1}{2 R_t} dt + dW_t\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact transition density and CDF via non-central \(\chi^2\) distribution \( rac{X_t}{t} \sim \chi^2(\delta, rac{x_0}{t})\), exact closed-form cumulants \(\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \kappa_4\) to arbitrary order, exact Laplace transform \(\mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda X_t}] = (1 + 2\lambda t)^{-\delta/2} \exp\left(- rac{\lambda x_0}{1 + 2\lambda t} ight)\), exact continuous characteristic function \(\phi(u; t)\), Feller boundary classification at 0 (entrance for \(\delta \ge 2\), reflecting for \(0 < \delta < 2\), absorbing for \(\delta = 0\)), exact Bessel process confluent hypergeometric moments \(\mathbb{E}[R_t]\), and exact path simulation with zero time discretization error. References: Feller (1951); Pitman & Yor (1982); Revuz & Yor (1999).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_besq and sample_bessel exact path simulators using scaled non-central chi-squared increments.
  • zoo/beyond/schobel_zhu.py — SchobelZhuProcess (SchobelZhu, SchobelZhuModel, SZModel): Schöbel-Zhu (1999) stochastic volatility model: \(dS_t = (r - q) S_t dt + \sigma_t S_t dW_t^S, \quad d\sigma_t = \kappa ( heta - \sigma_t) dt + au dW_t^\sigma\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Gaussian volatility dynamics with non-negative instantaneous variance \(v_t = \sigma_t^2\), exact continuous characteristic function, Gil-Pelaez European Call and Put pricing satisfying exact Put-Call parity, Black-Scholes implied volatility smile inversion, and coupled vectorized path simulation. References: Schöbel & Zhu (1999); Lord & Kahl (2007).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_schobel_zhu simulator supporting coupled asset and volatility paths.
  • zoo/beyond/black_karasinski.py — BlackKarasinskiProcess (BlackKarasinski, BKProcess, BKModel): Black-Karasinski (1991) lognormal short-rate model: \(d(\ln r_t) = a(b - \ln r_t) dt + \sigma dW_t, \quad r_t = \exp(x_t) > 0\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Guarantees strictly positive interest rates across all horizons. Features exact Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Gaussian conditional moments for log-rate \(x_t = \ln(r_t)\), exact short-rate lognormal conditional and stationary moments, Monte Carlo zero-coupon bond pricing \(P(0, T)\) and yield curve \(y(0, T)\), and exact path simulation without discretization error for \(x_t\). References: Black & Karasinski (1991); Brigo & Mercurio (2006).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_black_karasinski simulator supporting exact log-rate transitions.
  • zoo/levy/gh.py — GeneralizedHyperbolicProcess (GH, GHProcess, GeneralizedHyperbolic): Generalized Hyperbolic (GH) Lévy process of Barndorff-Nielsen (1977) and Eberlein & Prause (2002): infinite-activity pure-jump Lévy process generated by the 5-parameter Generalized Hyperbolic distribution \(GH(\lambda, \alpha, eta, \delta, \mu)\) under EXACT exactness level. Features exact characteristic exponent \(\psi(u)\) with modified Bessel \(K_\lambda\) functions, exact cumulants \(\kappa_1, \dots, \kappa_4\) derived from underlying GIG subordinator moments, Lévy triplet \((b, 0, u)\), Gil-Pelaez European Call and Put pricing with exact Put-Call parity, implied volatility smile inversion, subfamily classification (NIG, Hyperbolic, Hyperbolic Cosine), and vectorized simulation via exact Inverse Gaussian subordination and Gil-Pelaez CDF inversion. References: Barndorff-Nielsen (1977); Barndorff-Nielsen & Halgreen (1977); Eberlein & Prause (2002).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_gh simulator supporting exact NIG subordination and Gil-Pelaez inversion.
  • zoo/beyond/sabr.py — SABRProcess (SABRModel, SABR): SABR (Stochastic Alpha, Beta, Rho) stochastic volatility model of Hagan et al. (2002): \(dF_t = \alpha_t F_t^ eta dW_t^F, \quad d\alpha_t = u \alpha_t dW_t^\alpha\) with \(\mathbb{E}[dW_t^F dW_t^\alpha] = ho dt\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features Hagan et al. (2002) asymptotic Black-76 implied volatility closed form with Obłój (2008) corrections, at-the-money (ATM) volatility formula, Black-76 European Call and Put pricing satisfying Put-Call parity, exact forward and log-normal volatility moments, smile backbone classification, and coupled vectorized simulation via log-Euler and Euler schemes. References: Hagan, Kumar, Lesniewski, & Woodward (2002); Obłój (2008).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_sabr simulator supporting coupled forward price and stochastic volatility paths.
  • zoo/beyond/hull_white.py — HullWhiteProcess (HullWhite, HW1F, ExtendedVasicek): Hull-White (1990) one-factor Gaussian short-rate model (extended Vasicek): \(dr_t = a(b - r_t) dt + \sigma dW_t\) with mean-reversion speed \(a > 0\), volatility \(\sigma > 0\), and long-term target rate \(b \in \mathbb{R}\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact zero-coupon bond pricing \(P(t, T) = A(t, T) \exp(-B(t, T) r_t)\), spot yield curve, instantaneous forward rates, conditional short rate and integrated rate moments, autocovariance, Jamshidian (1989) closed-form European bond Call and Put options with exact Put-Call parity, caplets and floorlets, and exact path simulation without time discretization error. References: Hull & White (1990, 1993); Jamshidian (1989); Vasicek (1977).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_hull_white simulator with exact Gaussian transitions and Euler fallback.
  • zoo/beyond/bates.py — BatesProcess (BatesModel, Bates96, SVJ): Bates (1996) stochastic volatility with jumps model coupling the Heston (1993) CIR variance diffusion with Merton (1976) log-normal price jumps: \(dS_t = (\mu - q - \lambda ar{k}) S_t dt + \sqrt{V_t} S_t dW_t^S + S_{t-} (e^Y - 1) dN_t\), \(dV_t = \kappa ( heta - V_t) dt + \sigma_v \sqrt{V_t} dW_t^V\) with \(\mathbb{E}[dW^S dW^V] = ho dt\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features continuous Albrecher et al. (2007) characteristic function factored with compound Poisson jumps, drift compensator \(-\lambda ar{k}\), high-precision cumulants \(\kappa_1, \dots, \kappa_4\), European Call and Put pricing via Gil–Pelaez Fourier inversion, exact Put-Call parity, Black–Scholes implied volatility smile inversion, and vectorized path simulation via Lord et al. (2010) full-truncation CIR scheme and Poisson jump shocks. References: Bates (1996); Heston (1993); Albrecher et al. (2007); Lord et al. (2010).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_bates path simulator supporting both log-return \(X_t\) and instantaneous variance \(V_t\).
  • zoo/levy/kou.py — KouJumpDiffusion (KouProcess, Kou72, Kou02): Kou (2002) double exponential jump-diffusion process combining continuous Brownian motion with asymmetric double exponential jump shocks: \(X_t = \mu t + \sigma W_t + \sum_{i=1}^{N_t} Y_i\), \(f_Y(y) = p \eta_1 e^{-\eta_1 y}\mathbb{I}_{y \ge 0} + (1-p) \eta_2 e^{\eta_2 y}\mathbb{I}_{y < 0}\) under EXACT exactness level. Features exact closed-form Lévy triplet \((b, \sigma^2, u)\) with analytical truncated drift integral, characteristic exponent \(\psi(u)\), analytical cumulants of all orders \(n\), European Call and Put option pricing via Gil–Pelaez / Carr–Madan Fourier inversion, Put-Call parity, Black–Scholes implied volatility smile/skew inversion, and exact simulation with zero time discretization error. References: Kou (2002); Cont & Tankov (2004).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_kou exact path simulator with zero discretization error.
  • zoo/beyond/cev.py — CEVProcess (CEV, ConstantElasticityOfVariance): Constant Elasticity of Variance (CEV) local volatility diffusion process \(dS_t = \mu S_t dt + \sigma S_t^\gamma dW_t, S_0 = s_0 > 0\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness. Features state-dependent local return volatility \(\sigma_{ ext{loc}}(S) = \sigma S^{\gamma - 1}\), constant return variance elasticity \(2(\gamma - 1)\), boundary classification with absorbing zero (default / bankruptcy risk) for \(\gamma < 1\), exact European option pricing via Schroder's (1989) non-central chi-squared representation across equity leverage (\(\gamma < 1\)), geometric Brownian motion (\(\gamma = 1\)), and commodity inverse leverage (\(\gamma > 1\)) regimes, exact Put-Call parity, analytical absorption probability \(P(S_T = 0) = 1 - F_{\chi^2}(x; 1/(1-\gamma))\), transition CDF, analytical Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Vega), conditional moments (closed-form for \(\gamma \in \{0.5, 1.0\}\) and quadrature propagation for general \(\gamma\)), and vectorized path simulation. References: Cox (1975); Schroder (1989); Emanuel & MacBeth (1982); Choi & Wu (2021).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_cev simulation routine supporting second-order Milstein and Euler–Maruyama schemes with absorbing boundary conditions at zero and exact geometric Brownian motion for \(\gamma = 1\).
  • zoo/levy/merton.py — MertonJumpDiffusion (MertonProcess, Merton76): Merton (1976) jump-diffusion process combining continuous Brownian motion with normally distributed compound Poisson jump shocks: \(X_t = \mu t + \sigma W_t + \sum_{i=1}^{N_t} Y_i\), \(Y_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_J, \sigma_J^2)\) under EXACT exactness level. Features exact Lévy triplet \((b, \sigma^2, u)\) with analytical truncated Gaussian drift integral, closed-form characteristic exponent, analytical cumulants of all orders \(n\), Merton (1976) analytical option pricing formula via Poisson mixture of Black–Scholes values, Put-Call parity, Black-Scholes implied volatility smile/skew inversion, and exact vectorized simulation with zero time discretization error. References: Merton (1976); Cont & Tankov (2004).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_merton exact path simulator with zero discretization error.
  • zoo/beyond/heston.py — HestonProcess (Heston): Continuous-time affine stochastic volatility diffusion model \(dX_t = (\mu - rac{1}{2}V_t)dt + \sqrt{V_t} dW_t^S\), \(dV_t = \kappa( heta - V_t)dt + \sigma_v \sqrt{V_t} dW_t^V\) with \(d\langle W^S, W^V angle_t = ho dt\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness. Features exact characteristic functions via Albrecher et al. (2007) continuous formulation, CIR instantaneous and integrated variance moments, Feller condition verification, analytical cumulants, European Call and Put option pricing via Gil-Pelaez Fourier inversion, Black-Scholes implied volatility smile/skew inversion via root-finding, and Full Truncation simulation (Lord et al. 2010). References: Heston (1993); Albrecher et al. (2007); Lord et al. (2010).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_heston simulation routine supporting Lord et al. (2010) Full Truncation scheme and truncated Euler scheme.
  • zoo/beyond/ornstein_uhlenbeck.py — OrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess (OrnsteinUhlenbeck, Vasicek): Continuous-time Gaussian mean-reverting diffusion \(dX_t = heta(\mu - X_t)dt + \sigma dW_t\) with MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact Gaussian transition density, exact conditional moments and cumulants, stationary distribution \(N(\mu, \sigma^2/(2 heta))\), relaxation time \( au = 1/ heta\), half-life \(t_{1/2} = \ln(2)/ heta\), exponential autocovariance and autocorrelation, two-time covariance, Lorentzian power spectral density \(S(\omega) = \sigma^2/(\pi( heta^2+\omega^2))\), exact Laplace transform and characteristic function, Vasicek zero-coupon bond pricing \(P( au) = A( au)e^{-B( au)r_0}\), yield curves, and asymptotic long-term yield. References: Uhlenbeck & Ornstein (1930); Vasicek (1977).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_ou supporting exact Gaussian increments without discretization bias (method="exact") and Euler–Maruyama discretisation (method="euler").
  • zoo/beyond/cir.py — CIRProcess (CoxIngersollRoss): Cox–Ingersoll–Ross square-root diffusion process \(dr_t = \kappa( heta - r_t)dt + \sigma\sqrt{r_t}dW_t\) with MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features Feller condition evaluation (\(2\kappa heta \ge \sigma^2\)), exact non-central chi-squared transition density and exact simulation via sample_cir, exact conditional moments and cumulants of all orders, stationary Gamma distribution properties, exponential autocovariance, exact Laplace transform and characteristic function, zero-coupon bond pricing \(P( au) = A( au)e^{-B( au)r_0}\) via the Riccati system, yield curves, and asymptotic long-term yield. References: Cox, Ingersoll & Ross (1985); Feller (1951).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_cir supporting exact non-central chi-squared transition sampling (method="exact"), full-truncation Euler–Maruyama (method="truncated_euler"), and reflected Euler–Maruyama (method="reflected_euler").
  • zoo/levy/compound_poisson.py — CompoundPoisson: general compound Poisson process with homogeneous Poisson arrival counter and parameterised jump distributions (NormalJump, ExponentialJump, DoubleExponentialJump, UniformJump, DiscreteJump). EXACT exactness level with closed-form Lévy triplet (b=λ·E[Y·𝟙_{|Y|≤1}], σ²=0, ν=λ·F_Y), exact characteristic function φ(u;t) = exp(λt(φ_Y(u)-1)), exact cumulants of all orders κ_n = λ·t·E[Yⁿ], and vectorized exact Poisson thinning simulation. References: Kingman (1993); Cont & Tankov (2004) Sec. 3.4; Sato (1999) Ex. 8.4.
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_compound_poisson using np.repeat and np.bincount with fallback for non-vectorized custom samplers.
  • zoo/beyond/mmpp.py — MarkovModulatedPoissonProcess: N-state MMPP (CTMC-modulated Poisson counts). MOMENT_PROPAGATION; no Levy triplet (dependent increments). Exact event-driven simulation, finite-horizon mean/variance and cumulants of any order via block matrix exponentials (with a conditioning guard), stationary distribution and mean intensity. Reference: Fischer & Meier-Hellstern (1993), Performance Evaluation 18, 149-171.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Minimum NumPy raised to numpy>=2.0. The library uses np.trapezoid, which does not exist in NumPy 1.x, so the old numpy>=1.24 lower bound allowed broken installs.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• rough/riccati.py — FractionalRiccatiSolver: corrected the sign of the linear Riccati coefficient to \((i\rho\nu u - \lambda)\), and the characteristic function now uses \(V_0 I^{1-\alpha}h(T) = V_0\int_0^T F(u, h(s))\,ds\) (El Euch & Rosenbaum 2019). It reduces to the classical Heston closed form at \(H = 1/2\).
  • rough/rbergomi.py — RoughBergomi simulates the Riemann–Liouville driver and its Brownian motion jointly and exactly (Cholesky), so \(\rho\) now correlates returns with variance and \(\mathbb E[v_t] = \xi_0\). theoretical_short_time_skew gains the missing \(1/(H + 3/2)\) factor (Fukasawa). Added FractionalKernel.volterra_joint_covariance and sample_volterra_cholesky.
  • signature/kernel.py — the Goursat solver weighted the increment term by 5/4. It is now the second-order trapezoidal scheme, converging to \(I_0(2)\) for \(X = Y = t\).
  • signature/algebra.py — level-3 log-signature Hall coordinates were twice their true value. log_signature_dimension computes the Möbius function exactly; the old lookup table stopped at \(n = 6\), which gave wrong Witt dimensions from depth 10.
  • calibration/surface/{heston,bates,double_heston}.py — the share-measure probability \(P_1\) normalised \(\varphi(u - i)\) by \(S_0\) instead of \(\varphi(-i) = S_0e^{rT}\), so every call price was wrong when \(r \ne 0\). Regression tests now check against the Black–Scholes and Merton limits.
  • calibration/filter/particle_filter.py — BootstrapParticleFilter discarded the previous weights on steps without resampling. Weights are now carried forward, and the incremental likelihood is \(\log\sum_i w_{k-1}^i p(y_k \mid x_k^i)\). Checked against the exact Kalman log-likelihood.
  • calibration/mle/hac.py — newey_west_hac(kernel="quadratic_spectral") silently used Bartlett weights. It now implements the Andrews (1991) kernel and rejects unknown kernels.
  • scripts/extract_changelog.py — the release workflow's note extractor did not match bracketed Keep a Changelog headings (## [X.Y.Z] — date), so GitHub releases got the placeholder body Release X.Y.Z.

docs.title: 1. Overview and Core Philosophy
docs.text:
In quantitative finance, models have historically been siloed across distinct libraries: - One implementation for closed-form analytics (e.g. characteristic function quadrature). - Another implementation for Monte Carlo simulation paths. - Finite difference routines for Greek sensitivities. - Specialized optimization loops for model calibration.

spxa.graph solves this fragmentation by treating stochastic processes, analytical transforms, payoff functions, and risk metrics as nodes in a shared Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). A stochastic model is defined once; the execution engine then dynamically routes evaluation across: 1. Analytical Backend: Closed-form solutions and exact moments. 2. Numerical Backend: Fourier transforms (Carr-Madan, Lewis, Cosine methods). 3. Simulation Backend: Pathwise Monte Carlo sampling. 4. Accelerated Backend: Vectorized batch evaluation across thousands of strikes and maturities. 5. Autodiff Tape: Exact, zero-truncation sensitivities (Delta, Gamma, Vega, Rho, Theta) via reverse-mode vector-Jacobian products (VJPs) and forward-mode dual numbers.

docs.title: A. European Option Pricing and Automated Greeks
docs.text:
from spxa.graph import (
    build_black_scholes_pricing_graph,
    compute_graph_greeks,
)

# Build a Black-Scholes pricing DAG
graph = build_black_scholes_pricing_graph(
    s0=100.0,
    k=100.0,
    t=1.0,
    r=0.05,
    sigma=0.2,
    is_call=True,
)

# Evaluate closed-form analytical price
results = graph.evaluate()
print("Call Price:", results["price"])

# Compute exact Greeks via reverse-mode autodiff tape
greeks = compute_graph_greeks(graph)
print("Delta:", greeks["delta"])
print("Gamma:", greeks["gamma"])
print("Vega :", greeks["vega"])
print("Theta:", greeks["theta"])
print("Rho  :", greeks["rho"])

docs.title: B. Graph-Based Model Calibration
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from spxa.graph import (
    ComputationalGraph,
    GraphCalibrator,
    MSELossNode,
    ParameterNode,
)

# Build parameter recovery problem
param_a = ParameterNode(value=0.0, name="slope")
param_b = ParameterNode(value=0.0, name="intercept")

# Setup synthetic targets
x_data = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 50)
y_target = 3.5 * x_data + 1.2

calibrator = GraphCalibrator()
loss_node = MSELossNode(prediction_node=..., target=y_target)

docs.title: 4. Graph Optimization Passes
docs.text: The GraphCompiler optimizes the DAG before execution: - Constant Folding: Subgraphs depending purely on ConstantNode are pre-evaluated at compile time. - Common Subexpression Elimination (CSE): Identical mathematical operations with identical inputs are merged into single nodes. - Dead Code Elimination: Pruning of nodes unreferenced by any downstream target. - Execution Caching: Thread-safe evaluation cache for instant reuse of stationary nodes.

docs.title: 5. Universal Implementation Layer (spxa.graph.adapters)
docs.text: Rather than requiring manually handwritten graph nodes for every one of the ~200 processes in spxa.zoo or objects in other submodules, spxa.graph provides an automatic reflection and adaptation layer:

docs.title: A. Zero-Boilerplate Zoo Process Adaptation
docs.text:
Any process from spxa.zoo (e.g. BatesModel, VarianceGamma, NIG, CIRProcess, BNSModel, etc.), as well as any composed process (\(X + Y\), \(c \cdot X\), \(X @ T\)), can be directly used in computational graphs:

from spxa.zoo import BatesModel, VarianceGamma

# 1. Any zoo process immediately has .to_graph()
bates = BatesModel(v0=0.04, kappa=2.0, theta=0.04, sigma_v=0.3, rho=-0.5)
bates_node = bates.to_graph()

# 2. Parameters are automatically discovered and mutable
bates_node.params["v0"].value = 0.05
bates_node.sync_parameters_to_process()

# 3. Graph nodes for simulation and characteristic function are auto-generated
cf_node = bates_node.char_func_node(u=0.5, t=1.0)
sim_node = bates_node.simulate_node(t=1.0, n_paths=1000, n_steps=100)

docs.title: B. Submodule Integration (risk, diff, calculus, copula)
docs.text:
• Risk Instruments (spxa.risk): Instruments (EuropeanOption, BarrierOption, AsianOption) and Portfolio have .to_graph() returning automated payoff and sensitivity aggregation graphs.
  • Differentiable SDEs (spxa.diff): DifferentiableSDE models have .to_graph() providing drift, diffusion, and Euler step graph nodes.
  • Copulas (spxa.copula): Copulas have .to_graph() providing coupled uniform sampling nodes.
  • Generators (spxa.calculus): InfinitesimalGenerator adapts into graph operator nodes evaluating \(\mathcal{A} f(x)\).

docs.title: 6. Deep Mathematical Calculus on Stochastic Processes
docs.text: The computational graph serves as a first-class algebraic engine for advanced stochastic calculus:

docs.title: A. Automated Itô Lemma (ItoTransformNode)
docs.text: Applies Itô's Lemma to derive the exact SDE of \(Y_t = f(X_t, t)\) automatically using graph derivatives: $\(dY_t = \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} + \mu \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} + \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2 \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2}\right) dt + \sigma \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} dW_t\)$

docs.title: B. Measure Changes (GirsanovTransformNode, EsscherTransformNode)
docs.text:
• Girsanov Drift Shifts: Shifts diffusion drift under market price of risk \(\lambda(x, t)\): \(\mu^\mathbb{Q} = \mu^\mathbb{P} - \sigma \lambda\).
  • Esscher Transforms: Shifts characteristic exponents for jump processes: \(\Psi_\theta(u) = \Psi(u - i\theta) - \Psi(-i\theta)\).

docs.title: C. Bochner Subordination & Cumulant Generation (BochnerSubordinationNode, AutomatedCumulantNode)
docs.text:
• Composes parent Lévy exponent with subordinator Laplace exponent: \(\Psi_Z(u) = -\Phi_T(-\Psi_X(u))\).
  • Automatically extracts cumulants \(\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \kappa_4\) to arbitrary order by real central differentiation of the CGF \(K(s) = \Psi(-is)\).

docs.title: D. Infinitesimal Generators & Martingale Verification (InfinitesimalGeneratorNode, MartingaleVerificationNode)
docs.text:
• Evaluates Dynkin's formula \(\mathcal{A} f(x) = \mu(x) f'(x) + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2(x) f''(x)\).
  • Algebraically checks whether \(f(X_t)\) is a true martingale by proving \(\mathcal{A} f(x) \equiv 0\) across the state space.

docs.title: E. Speed / Scale Density & Feller Boundary Classification (ScaleDensityNode, SpeedDensityNode, FellerBoundaryClassifierNode)
docs.text:
• Computes scale density \(s(x) = \exp\left(-\int \frac{2\mu}{\sigma^2}\right)\) and speed density \(m(x) = \frac{1}{\sigma^2 s}\).
  • Classifies 1D diffusion boundaries into Feller types: Regular, Exit, Entrance, or Natural.

docs.title: F. Malliavin Calculus & Bismut Integration by Parts (MalliavinBismutDeltaNode)
docs.text:
• Simulates the first variation process \(Y_t = \partial X_t / \partial x_0\) alongside \(X_t\).
  • Evaluates pathwise Bismut weights \(\pi_T = \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T \frac{Y_t}{\sigma(X_t)} dW_t\), computing exact Greek sensitivities of discontinuous payoffs without payoff mollification.

docs.title: 7. Advanced Stochastic Foundations
docs.text: The engine includes three theoretical pillars bridging stochastic analysis and computational graphs:

docs.title: A. Semimartingale Decomposition Wires & Algebra (spxa.graph.semimartingale)
docs.text: In continuous-time stochastic calculus, semimartingales form the largest class of processes with respect to which stochastic integrals can be defined. - Typed Semimartingale Wires (SemimartingaleWire): Graph edges carry continuous-time processes decomposed into their canonical components: $\(X_t = X_0 + A_t + M_t^c + J_t\)$ where \(A_t\) is continuous of finite variation, \(M_t^c\) is a continuous local martingale, and \(J_t\) is a pure jump process. - Quadratic Covariation Operator (QuadraticCovariationNode): Computes the pathwise and predictable bracket \([X, Y]_t\) and \(\langle X^c, Y^c \rangle_t\): $\([X, Y]_t = \lim_{|\Pi| \to 0} \sum_{i} (X_{t_{i+1}} - X_{t_i})(Y_{t_{i+1}} - Y_{t_i})\)$ - Stochastic Product & Integration by Parts (StochasticProductNode): Evaluates the product \(Z_t = X_t Y_t\) verifying the stochastic integration by parts formula: $\(d(X_t Y_t) = X_{t-} dY_t + Y_{t-} dX_t + d[X, Y]_t\)$ achieving machine-precision bracket balance (\(\epsilon \sim 10^{-15}\)). - Predictable Itô Integrals (StochasticIntegralNode): Computes \((H \cdot X)_t = \int_0^t H_s dX_s\) with exact Itô isometry \(\mathbb{E}[(H \cdot M)_t^2] = \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^t H_s^2 d\langle M \rangle_s\right]\).

docs.title: B. Four-Facet Representation Duality Engine (spxa.graph.duality)
docs.text:
Processes are mathematically dual across four equivalent representations: 1. SDE Facet (SDEFacet): \(dX_t = \mu(X_t) dt + \sigma(X_t) dW_t + J_t\). 2. Infinitesimal Generator Facet (GeneratorFacet): \(\mathcal{A} f(x) = \mu(x) f'(x) + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2(x) f''(x)\). 3. Fourier Characteristic Exponent Facet (FourierFacet): \(\mathbb{E}[e^{i u X_t}] = \exp(t \Psi(u))\). 4. Speed / Scale Density Facet (DensityFacet): Invariant measure \(\pi(x) \propto m(x)\).

The ProcessDualityCore automatically synthesizes missing representations: - Given an SDE, derives the infinitesimal generator and speed/scale density. - Given an infinitesimal generator, inverts for the drift \(\mu(x) = \mathcal{A}(\text{id})(x)\) and diffusion \(\sigma^2(x) = \mathcal{A}(x^2) - 2x\mathcal{A}(x)\). - Lévy-Khintchine Triplet Compiler (compile_levy_khintchine, triplet_to_fourier_facet): Directly compiles arbitrary triplets \((b, \sigma^2, \nu)\) into executable characteristic exponents: $\(\Psi(u) = i b u - \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2 u^2 + \int_{\mathbb{R}} \left( e^{i u y} - 1 - i u y \mathbf{1}_{|y|\le 1} \right) \nu(dy)\)$

docs.title: C. Algebraic Process Surgery Operators (spxa.graph.surgery)
docs.text: Advanced operators that transform stochastic paths and boundary conditions algebraically: - Doléans Exponential & Stochastic Logarithm (DoleansExponentialNode, StochasticLogarithmNode): Computes the stochastic exponential martingale: $\(\mathcal{E}(X)_t = \exp\left(X_t - X_0 - \frac{1}{2}\langle X^c \rangle_t\right) \prod_{s \le t} (1 + \Delta X_s) e^{-\Delta X_s}\)$ and its inverse, the stochastic logarithm \(\mathcal{L}(Z)_t = \int \frac{dZ_s}{Z_{s-}}\). - Tanaka Decomposition & Local Time Extraction (TanakaDecompositionNode): Decomposes positive convex envelopes and isolates local time \(L_t^a(X)\) at strike \(a\): $\((X_t - a)^+ = (X_0 - a)^+ + \int_0^t \mathbf{1}_{\{X_s > a\}} dX_s + \frac{1}{2} L_t^a(X)\)$ - Doob \(h\)-Transform (DoobHTransformNode): Conditions diffusion paths on staying in a sub-domain or reaching a target via excessive harmonic functions \(h\): $\(\mu^h(t, x) = \mu(t, x) + \sigma^2(t, x) \frac{h'(x)}{h(x)}\)$ (e.g., standard Brownian motion conditioned to stay positive produces the 3D Bessel process drift \(1/x\)). - Stratonovich \(\leftrightarrow\) Itô Conversion (StratonovichToItoNode, ItoToStratonovichNode): Transitions between Itô and Stratonovich calculus by adding or subtracting the midpoint drift correction \(\frac{1}{2}\sigma(x)\sigma'(x)\).

docs.title: 8. Statistical Information Geometry & Manifold Calibration (spxa.geom, spxa.graph.geom)
docs.text: Information geometry equips stochastic process parameter spaces \(\mathcal{M} = \{\theta \in \Theta\}\) with intrinsic Riemannian manifolds rather than flat Euclidean spaces:

docs.title: A. Fisher Information Metric (FIM)
docs.text: The Fisher metric tensor measures informational distance between stochastic transition densities: $\(g_{ij}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_\theta \left[ \frac{\partial \log p}{\partial \theta_i} \frac{\partial \log p}{\partial \theta_j} \right] = - \mathbb{E}_\theta \left[ \frac{\partial^2 \log p}{\partial \theta_i \partial \theta_j} \right]\)$ - Exact Closed Forms: Computed analytically for Gaussians \(g = \text{diag}(1/\sigma^2, 2/\sigma^2)\) and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck transition densities. - Numerical & Empirical Score Covariance: Automatically evaluated via finite-difference Hessians and pathwise score vectors.

docs.title: B. Connections & Geodesic Flow
docs.text:
• Levi-Civita Connection & Christoffel Symbols: \(\Gamma^k_{ij}(\theta) = \frac{1}{2} g^{kl} (\partial_i g_{jl} + \partial_j g_{il} - \partial_l g_{ij})\).
  • Amari \(\alpha\)-Connections: \(\Gamma^{(\alpha), k}_{ij} = \Gamma^k_{ij} - \frac{\alpha}{2} g^{kl} T_{ijl}\) where \(T_{ijl}\) is the skewness tensor (\(\alpha = 0\) Riemannian, \(\alpha = 1\) exponential, \(\alpha = -1\) mixture).
  • Rao Hyperbolic Distance (GeodesicFlow): Integrates geodesic paths \(\ddot{\theta}^k + \Gamma^k_{ij} \dot{\theta}^i \dot{\theta}^j = 0\) via shooting solvers to measure true model distance \(d_R(\theta_1, \theta_2) = \int \sqrt{g_{ij} \dot{\theta}^i \dot{\theta}^j} dt\).

docs.title: C. Natural Gradient Optimization (NaturalGradientCalibratorNode)
docs.text: Replaces naive Euclidean gradient descent with Riemannian manifold updates: $\( ilde{ abla}_ heta \mathcal{L} = g^{-1}( heta) abla_ heta \mathcal{L}, \quad heta_{t+1} = heta_t - \eta ilde{ abla}_ heta \mathcal{L}\)$ eliminating ill-conditioned ravines, Feller boundary sticking, and parameterization distortions.

docs.title: 9. Rough Paths & Tensor Signature Calculus (spxa.signature, spxa.graph.signature)
docs.text: Path signatures provide a non-parametric, coordinate-free encoding of continuous and jump paths:

docs.title: A. Truncated Tensor Signature & Chen's Identity (PathSignature)
docs.text: For a multidimensional path \(X: [0, T] \to \mathbb{R}^d\), the truncated signature of order \(M\) is: $\(S(X)_{s,t}^{(M)} = \bigoplus_{k=0}^M \int_{s < u_1 < \dots < u_k < t} dX_{u_1} \otimes \dots \otimes dX_{u_k} \in T^{(M)}(\mathbb{R}^d)\)$ Satisfies Chen's multiplicative identity: $\(S(X)_{0,T} = S(X)_{0,t} \otimes S(X)_{t,T}\)$

docs.title: B. Shuffle Algebra & Free Lie Log-Signature (SignatureAlgebra)
docs.text:
• Shuffle Product: Iterated integrals multiply via shuffles: \(S^u \cdot S^v = \sum_{w \in u \sqcup v} S^w\).
  • Log-Signature Projection: Projects signatures onto the free Lie algebra \(\mathfrak{g}^{(M)}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) via Campbell-Baker-Hausdorff / Dynkin operators, reducing dimensionality according to Witt's formula (e.g. \(15 \to 5\) at depth 3 for 2D paths, a 66.7% compression without information loss).

docs.title: C. Signature Kernels via 2D Hyperbolic Goursat PDE (SignatureKernel)
docs.text: Computes the infinite-dimensional inner product \(K(X, Y) = \langle S(X), S(Y) \rangle\) without tensor truncation by solving the hyperbolic PDE: $\(\frac{\partial^2 K}{\partial s \partial t}(s, t) = K(s, t) \langle \dot{X}_s, \dot{Y}_t \rangle, \quad K(s, 0) = 1, \quad K(0, t) = 1\)$ Runs in polynomial \(O(N_X \cdot N_Y)\) time.

docs.title: D. Universal Linear Pricing (SignatureLinearPricerNode)
docs.text: Represents arbitrary path-dependent payoffs (Asian, lookbacks, barriers) as linear functionals on the expected signature: $\(\text{Price} \approx \langle \mathbf{w}, \mathbb{E}[S(X)_{0,T}] \rangle\)$

docs.title: 10. Rough Volatility & Volterra Stochastic Calculus (spxa.rough, spxa.graph.rough)
docs.text: Extends stochastic modeling to sub-diffusive, non-Markovian volatility surfaces:

docs.title: A. Fractional Singular Kernels & Hybrid Convolution (FractionalKernel)
docs.text:
• Riemann-Liouville fractional power kernel with Hurst exponent \(H \in (0, 1/2)\): $\(K_H(t) = \frac{\sqrt{2H}}{\Gamma(H + 1/2)} t^{H - 1/2}\)$
  • Bennedsen-Lunde-Pakkanen Hybrid Scheme: Decomposes \(\int_0^t (t-s)^{H-1/2} dW_s\) into exact analytic integration for the singular neighborhood \(s \approx t\) and FFT-accelerated convolution for the regular tail.
  • Exact Fractional Brownian Motion: Cholesky covariance sampling of \(R_H(t, s) = \frac{1}{2}(t^{2H} + s^{2H} - |t - s|^{2H})\).

docs.title: B. Rough Bergomi Model (RoughBergomi)
docs.text: Asset and variance dynamics: $\(S_t = S_0 \mathcal{E}\left( \int_0^t \sqrt{v_s} dW_s \right), \quad v_t = \xi_0 \exp\left( \eta \sqrt{2H} \tilde{W}_t^H - \frac{1}{2} \eta^2 t^{2H} \right)\)$ Reproduces the empirical power-law blow-up of short-time at-the-money implied volatility skews: $\(\psi(\tau) = \left|\frac{\partial \sigma_{BS}}{\partial k}\right|_{k=0} \approx \frac{|\rho| \eta}{2} \frac{\sqrt{2H}}{H + 1/2} \tau^{H - 1/2}\)$

docs.title: C. Fractional Adams-Bashforth-Moulton Riccati Solver (FractionalRiccatiSolver)
docs.text: Solves the non-local fractional Riccati Volterra integral equation: $\(h(t) = \int_0^t \frac{(t-s)^{H-1/2}}{\Gamma(H + 1/2)} F(u, h(s)) ds\)$ providing exact, highly stable characteristic functions \(\mathbb{E}[e^{i u X_T}]\) for the Rough Heston model.

docs.title: Contributing to spxa
docs.text:
spxa is research infrastructure for stochastic process algebra. Correctness and mathematical honesty are non-negotiable. Every contribution must be grounded in a published result, and the library must never silently return an incorrect answer.

This document is the authoritative guide for every type of contribution. Read the section for what you want to add, then follow it exactly.

By participating in this project you agree to abide by the Code of Conduct. Security vulnerabilities must be reported privately as described in the Security Policy, never through public issues.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Nityahapani/spxa.git
cd spxa
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pre-commit install

Dev dependencies: pytest, pytest-cov, sympy, numpy, scipy, ruff, mypy, pre-commit.

Run the full test suite before and after any change:

python -m pytest tests/ -q

All 235+ tests must pass. Never submit a PR that breaks existing tests.
